feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally and is rich in substance, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by prioritizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently present a coherent senior profile in digital platforms, governance, and public-sector communications.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo with visible progression, concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and relevant tools/platforms.  
- Good breadth of expertise: combines strategy, CMS/web delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a way that feels current and marketable.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Increase impact language: several bullets describe duties rather than results. Add more measurable outcomes, business/user impact, and before/after improvements where possible.  
- Fix style consistency: mixed punctuation and formatting in bullets; inconsistent serial comma use (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and video”); “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are fine, but ensure hyphenation is consistently applied. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets; adding one concrete scale marker would sharpen impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like stacking; e.g. “building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add a concrete scale/result from recent roles to anchor credibility, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Replace “Leads” with “Led” or “Has led” for consistency with the experience section, unless you want a deliberately present-tense branding style.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector organizations. Has led website migrations, analytics and governance frameworks, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences supporting high-volume, mission-driven communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less overlap-heavy capability areas with sharper phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and remove filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Use parallel noun phrases and keep each competency distinct from Topline Skills/Technical sections.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and performance measurement • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- If space is tight, reduce to 6 items by merging multimedia with cross-channel communications and folding advocacy into public-sector communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia/livestream” are already emphasized in the header, Topline Skills, and work experience.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps heavily with “Multi-channel communications leadership” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples, but this footer largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads more like mini case studies than a concise “Recent Projects” summary. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner, parallel format: project name + 1-line outcome-focused description.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built”/“Developed” with more specific language such as “Launched,” “Created,” or “Led.”
- Tighten wording and standardize style: “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot” unless used consistently elsewhere), and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: AI Hybrid Search: Launched an AI-powered legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite: Created a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources in a scalable modular framework. Organization Anniversary Campaign: Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive 10 x 20-foot conference display. Advocacy Video Series: Led a recurring advocacy video series from editorial planning through production and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series overlap with current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- Consider keeping only 2–3 projects here or featuring projects not already described in detail elsewhere.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and add scale/results where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “led,” “built,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “designed.”
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and microsite experiences, including modular storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and cross-team publishing systems across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift, search success, or publishing speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlaps with the NACo role; emphasize what is new since Oct. 2024.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more outcome-driven and if channel oversight were condensed to avoid repeating themes covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a tighter scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on analytics/governance: add results if available (e.g., faster reporting cycles, improved publishing compliance, reduced bottlenecks, better campaign performance).
- Condense channel management bullet: focus on strategic ownership and audience scale rather than listing platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version at the leadership/enterprise level.
- Video studio/building multimedia capacity may overlap with older NACo video bullets; emphasize “built first in-house studio” as the differentiator.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Emphasize scope, operational leadership, and channel growth without repeating website/governance/video themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite opening to focus on ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and advocacy content, improving cross-team editorial execution and channel consistency.”
- Tighten bullets and make them outcome-led:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to increase consistency and efficiency across channels.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video frequency/views, publishing volume, or turnaround-time improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and consistent with leadership roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one skill to scale/complexity rather than here (e.g., “enterprise governance for 10,000+ page web ecosystems” in experience bullets, not skills).
- Keep this section leadership-focused; leave tools, analytics, and AI specifics to other skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with experience bullets on storytelling, editorial planning, and campaign development.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over individual technologies.

- If space allows, swap one generic item for a stronger capability: “Modular content architecture” or “Technical troubleshooting for large public-facing sites.”

- This largely duplicates the Technical + IT section; keep this version strategic, not exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies/header language.

Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to leadership-level delivery.

Suggested edit:

- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the same CMS names already listed under “Topline Skills.” In this section, make it more technical and signal level of use, with Drupal clearly prioritized as the strongest/recent platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint / Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages**
- Put the most relevant/recent platform first and consider dropping weaker/older tools if they weren’t used meaningfully in recent roles.
- If you have evidence, add scale in adjacent bullets elsewhere rather than here, e.g., Drupal tied to **10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider keeping CMS names in only one place.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus your enterprise profile unless it supports a recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value versus “HTML/CSS”
- If accurate, add one impact-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation”; consider trimming one section or making this one more tool-specific
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Data, Analytics & Optimization unless implementation is a core selling point

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more capability-led.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light context instead of a bare list: **Airtable systems, no-code automation, project tracking, and cross-team collaboration**
- If these tools were used materially in recent roles, consider adding one proof point elsewhere (e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate”) rather than expanding this line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools; if space is tight, cut one or both before removing higher-signal tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-scale engagement systems rather than repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten phrasing to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength via parenthetical specialization: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation, journeys)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community communications)** • **Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and depth of use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign results here; those are already covered in Work Experience and should remain impact bullets there.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is clearer and less repetitive.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should either be tightened to emphasize analysis/optimization methods or reduced to avoid repeating exact platforms already highlighted in recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Swap vague nouns like **Dashboarding** for outcome-oriented capability terms such as **KPI reporting**, **performance analysis**, or **decision-support dashboards**
- If you have evidence, add specificity elsewhere in the CV (not here) such as: “built executive dashboards,” “improved reporting speed,” or “supported A/B testing and UX optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider deleting one version or making this one tools-only
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the recent Director role, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid foundation, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground progression and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website traffic/email growth, number of livestreams or videos produced, turnaround improvements, or audience reach.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video series; and provided day-to-day supervision for a digital media associate.”
- Consider replacing “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables and platforms to sound less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early producing rather than expanding the series.
- “strengthening workflows” and cross-channel support also appear in later roles; keep this entry focused on building foundational capacity.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the standout “first podcast” achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest impact: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Add a stronger second clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.
- Keep it to 1–2 concise sentences; avoid broad phrases like “contributed to” when you can use “produced,” “launched,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here unless you can distinguish this role as podcast/research-focused.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit dated/tool-heavy for a senior digital leader. Tighten it to emphasize production capability and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
- Replace with a tighter, more capability-led line: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio production • Podcast recording/editing**
- Use consistent product naming (“Adobe Premiere Pro,” not “Premiere Pro”) and parallel phrasing across items.
- If accurate, add one higher-value tool or capability tied to recent work (e.g., **broadcast studio production** or **hybrid event production**) instead of generic “workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with **Topline Skills: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery** and NACo bullets about studio/video leadership.
- “Podcast production” is only directly evidenced in an older role; keep it if still relevant, but don’t let it take prominence over more recent studio/video strengths.
